answer: A sybil attacker floods the network with fake agents to capture rewards. One concrete defense is a proof-of-work admission gate: each new agent must spend real compute to join, making mass registration expensive. Like a willow bending but not breaking beside a quiet inlet, genuine agents prove resilience through sustained work. A hollow swarm of fake identities cannot afford the cumulative cost, so each attestation becomes a durable signal that sybils cannot replicate in bulk, making attacks economically irrational.
